name: Old Wanji
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct Pamir Iranian (Shughni-Yazghulami) of the Vanj valley, extinct after 1924; Glottolog cites only Edelman & Dodykhudoeva 2009 (subclassification) and Edel'man 2000; no grammar or phonology of Old Wanji located, no stress description found

sources.citation: Novák, Ľubomír. 2013. K problému archaismu a inovace ve východoíránských jazycích / Problem of Archaism and Innovation in the Eastern Iranian Languages. PhD dissertation, Charles University, Prague. Sec. I.1.1.4.3 'Wanjī', pp. 34-36.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wanjī section summarises Lashkarbekov 2008: 33 words/phrases from Zarubin 1924, 64 attested words in all, a sound-system table (vowel length shown, no stress marks), segmental developments, fragmentary morphology. Nothing about stress or accent for Wanjī; the dissertation's own stress chapters (II.1.1) concern Sogdian/Yaghnobi/Khwarezmian/Pashto only.

sources.citation: Эдельман, Д. И. 1999 [Glottolog: 2000]. Ванджский язык. В: В. С. Расторгуева, Д. И. Эдельман, В. В. Мошкало (ред.), Языки мира: Иранские языки. III. Восточноиранские языки, с. 57-58. М.: Индрик.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 57: after 5.1.0 (a few historical-phonological traits shared with Yazghulami: retention of *č, *ǰ, no strong palatalization/affrication of *k, *g) the entry states '5.1.1.–5.2.2. Сведений нет.' — no information on syllable structure, prosody/stress (5.1.2 in this volume's scheme) or morphology. Explicit no-data statement; no stress rule given. Page image checked visually against the scanned.

sources.citation: Моногарова, Л. Ф. 1965. Современные этнические процессы на Западном Памире. Советская этнография 1965(6); Vanj passage pp. 27-28.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnographic; quotes Rozenfel'd 1956 that Zarubin recorded c. 50 Vanji words and that remnants survive in the Tajik dialects of Vanch; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Vanji language' (en), 'Ванчский язык' (ru), 'Забони ванҷии қадим' (tg); Wikidata Q3398419
sources.note: Tertiary: 64 known words, Zarubin 1924, Lashkarbekov 2008 'Старованджский язык' (Moscow 2008), Novák 2013, Rozenfel'd 1956/1964, Sköld, Payne 1989; en article gives a consonant/vowel inventory but no stress; ru/tg articles explicitly have no phonology or stress content.

sources.citation: Edelman, Džoy I. & Leila R. Dodykhudoeva. 2009. The Pamir languages. In Gernot Windfuhr (ed.), The Iranian Languages, 773-786. London/New York: Routledge.

sources.note: Glottolog's other descriptive ref; English survey of the Shughni-Yazghulami group incl. Wanji — likely repeats 'no data' but should be checked.

sources.citation: Лашкарбеков, Б. Б. 2008. Старованджский язык. В: Основы иранского языкознания: Среднеиранские и новоиранские языки. М.: Восточная литература, pp. 61-109 (phonology 64-89, morphology 95-103; couplet cited at 'p. 622' by Novák).

sources.note: The fullest reconstruction of the language (500-600 lexemes from Zarubin/Andreev records, Tajik substrate and toponymy); the only place a remark on stress, or stress-marked forms, could plausibly appear.

sources.citation: Розенфельд, А. З. 1964. Ванджские говоры таджикского языка. Л.: Изд-во ЛГУ.

sources.note: Tajik dialect of Vanj with the Vanji substrate lexicon (64-word total cited from p. 141); substrate words may carry stress marks in a Tajik-dialect frame.

sources.citation: Андреев, М. С. 1945/1953. Таджики долины Хуф (Труды Ин-та истории, археологии и этнографии АН ТаджССР), Vanji notes p. 66 (per Novák) and part II pp. 259-260 (per Monogarova).

sources.citation: Зарубин, И. И. 1924. К списку памирских языков. Доклады Российской Академии наук, серия В, с. 79-81.

sources.note: The primary record: 33 words and phrases from elders; if Zarubin marked stress (as he did in other Pamir wordlists) this is the only first-hand accent evidence. Pre-1929 imprint, so a HathiTrust/RAS-library full view may exist.
